title: Japan Told Him No 3 Times. He Saved Thousands Anyway
description: In 1940 a Japanese diplomat ignored his orders and wrote visas by hand until his train pulled away. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chiune_Sugihara Would you have risked your career for strangers? #anime #shorts #animestory #retroanime #truestory #history

characters.Chiune Sugihara: 40-year-old Japanese diplomat in 1940, short black hair neatly side-parted, clean-shaven, no glasses, no hat, dark gray 1940s three-piece wool suit, white shirt, dark tie, black fountain pen
characters.Yukiko Sugihara: 27-year-old Japanese woman in 1940, black hair in a low 1940s bun, no hat, navy-blue long-sleeve dress with a white collar, small pearl earrings
characters.Refugee father: 35-year-old Polish Jewish man in 1940, short brown beard, tired eyes, no hat, worn dark brown wool overcoat over a gray sweater, holding a small cardboard suitcase

scenes.say: In 1940, a Japanese diplomat's pen was the only way out for thousands. Chiune Sugihara opened his curtains in Kaunas, Lithuania, and saw families lined up outside his gate.
scenes.video: [0-4s] Inside Sugihara's quiet second-floor office in the Japanese consulate in Kaunas, early morning light, Chiune Sugihara pulls back a lace curtain. [4-7s] Over his shoulder through the window: a short line of tired families with suitcases waiting at the consulate's iron gate on a cobblestone street. [7-10s] Close-up of Chiune Sugihara's face, eyes narrowing, still holding the curtain.

scenes.say: They were Jewish families fleeing the war in Poland, and a Japanese transit visa was their last way out. But Tokyo's rule was clear: no papers, no visa.
scenes.video: [0-4s] At the iron gate of the consulate in Kaunas, the Refugee father holds his small daughter's hand, looking up at the building. [4-7s] Inside the consulate office, Chiune Sugihara sits at a dark wooden desk, a black fountain pen resting beside a closed telephone. [7-10s] Close-up of Chiune Sugihara's hand turning the fountain pen over slowly, not writing yet.

scenes.say: He asked Tokyo three times. Three times, the answer was no. So he talked it over with his wife, Yukiko, and on July 18 he picked up his pen anyway.
scenes.video: [0-4s] In the consulate office in Kaunas at night, Chiune Sugihara slowly puts down the black telephone receiver, lamp light on his face. [4-7s] In the small apartment kitchen upstairs in the consulate, Yukiko Sugihara sits across a wooden table from him and gives a small firm nod. [7-10s] Back at his desk, Chiune Sugihara uncaps the fountain pen, jaw set.

scenes.say: He wrote every visa by hand, 18 to 20 hours a day, turning out a normal month's work every single day, racing the Soviet order to close the consulate.
scenes.video: [0-4s] In the consulate office in Kaunas, Chiune Sugihara writes quickly at his desk, papers seen edge-on with no readable writing, the window behind him going from day to dark. [4-7s] The Refugee father stands in front of the desk, holding his breath, clutching his coat. [7-10s] Close-up of the Refugee father's eyes filling with tears as Chiune Sugihara slides a folded paper toward him.

scenes.say: On September 4 he had to leave. But at Kaunas station he kept writing, and as the train pulled out, he threw signed papers from the window into waiting hands.
scenes.video: [0-4s] On the platform of Kaunas railway station on a gray morning, a dark steam train waits, Yukiko Sugihara steps aboard. [4-7s] Inside the train compartment, Chiune Sugihara leans out the open window, still writing against the window frame with the fountain pen. [7-10s] Slow shot from the platform as the train starts moving and loose papers drift down into the Refugee father's raised hands.

scenes.say: In 1947, Japan's foreign ministry asked him to resign, and he sold light bulbs door to door. Today, up to 100,000 people are alive because of one diplomat's pen.
scenes.video: [0-4s] A quiet residential street in Fujisawa, Japan, late 1940s, Chiune Sugihara, older, in a plain coat, holds a small box of light bulbs at a wooden front door. [4-7s] Close-up of his face, calm, a small polite bow. [7-10s] Close-up of the old black fountain pen resting on a wooden table in warm evening light.
